categories.name: Phase 0 · The AI Engineer on the Edge
categories.description: Understand what an AI engineer actually ships — and the one concrete runtime (Workers, Workers AI, Vectorize, D1) every later phase builds on
outcomes: Explain how the AI-engineer role differs from ML engineer and data scientist
Name the Workers AI / Vectorize / D1 substrate each phase uses
Pick your entry point into the roadmap by experience level

categories.name: Phase 1 · Models & Inference on Workers AI
categories.description: Run real inference on pre-trained models — served from the edge through the Workers AI binding
outcomes: Call a Workers AI model and read its token and cost implications
Explain tokenization, attention and scaling laws in applied terms
Pick a model for a task by latency, cost and capability

categories.name: Phase 2 · Prompting & Structured Output
categories.description: Make model output reliable — prompts, tool/function calling, and schema-valid JSON from Workers AI
outcomes: Write system prompts and few-shot examples that hold under variation
Drive function/tool calls from a Worker
Ship a Structured Data Extractor: text in, schema-validated JSON out (Portfolio L1)

categories.name: Phase 3 · Embeddings & RAG on Vectorize
categories.description: Ground answers in your own data — embeddings and retrieval on Vectorize with D1 metadata
outcomes: Embed and index a corpus with CloudflareWorkersAIEmbeddings
Tune chunking and retrieval strategies, then measure them
Ship a Document Q&A System with citations and a faithfulness/relevance eval (Portfolio L1)

categories.name: Phase 4 · Agents, Memory & Orchestration
categories.description: Build agents that reason and act — LangGraph checkpointed on D1, long-term memory on Vectorize, durable on Workers
outcomes: Build a tool-using agent loop with persistent memory
Checkpoint and resume graphs on D1; orchestrate with Durable Objects, Queues & Workflows
Ship a Multi-Source Research Agent reusing Phase 2 tool calls and Phase 3 retrieval (Portfolio L2)

categories.name: Phase 5 · Evals, Safety & Observability
categories.description: Prove it works and ships safely — evals, red-teaming, guardrails, and AI Gateway observability
outcomes: Build an eval suite (benchmarks + LLM-as-judge) that gates a model change
Add guardrails and mitigate hallucination and bias
Ship an eval + red-team + observability harness over your Phase 4 agent (Portfolio L3)

categories.name: Phase 6 · Ship on Cloudflare
categories.description: Take it to production on the edge — deploy, scale, cost-control, and CI/CD with Wrangler
outcomes: Deploy and scale on Workers with Wrangler
Cap inference cost and wire CI/CD-gated evals
Ship a cost-bounded, observable AI feature to production (e.g. an AI Code Review Bot)

categories.name: Appendix · Fine-tuning & Training
categories.description: Optional track — customize models with LoRA, RLHF and dataset curation when prompting is not enough
outcomes: Decide when fine-tuning beats prompting, with a measured comparison
Fine-tune with LoRA/QLoRA on a curated dataset
Ship a domain-tuned assistant wrapped in a safety stack (Portfolio L3, senior signal)

categories.name: Appendix · Other Clouds & Platforms
categories.description: Optional track — GCP, Docker and Kubernetes for portability and comparison off the Cloudflare path
outcomes: Map Workers concepts onto GCP equivalents
Containerize a service with Docker
Run a workload on Kubernetes

categories.name: Appendix · Engineering & Communication
categories.description: Optional track — software-engineering foundations (SOLID, ACID, SQL, CI/CD) plus LlamaIndex and communication
outcomes: Apply SOLID design and ACID guarantees
Reason about microservices, SQL joins and CI/CD
Communicate technical work with structure and presence
